section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1974
title: The volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population did not reveal and definite trend over the period 1967-74. It was only during 1971-73 that accidental deaths per one lakh of population declined in comparison to earlier four years. During 1974, the volume of accidental deaths increased. From 18.5 accidental deaths per one lakh of population in 1973, it went up to 18.9 per one lakh of population in 1974. notes: Volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population in the States, Union Territories & Metropolitan Cities

The volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population for the States as a whole for 1974 was 18.67. For Union Territories, it was 34.87 and the all-India average was 18.88. The Maximum volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was 42.12 for Metropolitan cities.
The range of volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population for States, Union Territories and Metropolitan cities was between 69.11 to 3.39.

The volume of accidental deaths was invariably more for metropolitan cities. Although, no direct reason could be assigned for such a vast variation in the volume of accidental deaths but difference in topography of different areas, population, level of industrialisation and other socio-economic factors could explain the variation. Among States, the volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was the maximum for Maharashtra(44.02), followed by Madhya Pradesh(31.24), Gujarat(20.94) and Karnataka(20.29). For other States the volume of accidental deaths ranged between 18.59 to 3.39. The minimum volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was for the State of Manipur(3.39).

The volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population for the Union Territories as a whole was 34.87. The maximum was for A & N Islands (69.11) while the minimum of 5.88 was for Laksha-dweep. Only three Union Territories registered less accidental deaths per one lakh of population than the all India average. These were Mizoram (9.86), Arunachal Pradesh(5.99) and Lakshadweep(5.88).
